content.jointProblem: Which combination of weld condition, service loading, temperature history and condensation explains cracking in AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor joints, and could changes to welding, filler or joint geometry reduce it? The first experiment would compare production-representative joints under measured service loading at room temperature and 2–6 °C, with controlled thermal and moisture conditions informed by field records and failed-section examination, to test whether the researcher’s thermo-mechanical fatigue methods transfer to this application.

rationale.text: Erić has directly investigated interacting mechanical fatigue and thermal cycling in welded structural steel, providing a relevant basis for testing the company’s suspected combined-loading mechanism.

sources.quote: Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF, with twelve specimens per programme.

rationale.text: He has experience translating measured industrial loads and temperatures into welded-structure fatigue assessments.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: His residual-stress measurement and modelling work supports investigating how weld condition contributes to crack development rather than attributing failure to temperature alone.

sources.quote: Residual stress relaxation in S355 cruciform fillet-welded joints was tracked over 10, 100, 1000, and 10 000 fatigue cycles
A cyclic plasticity FE model employing a Chaboche kinematic hardening rule reproduced the surface relaxation trend within 12% across all conditions.

rationale.text: His group reports relevant fatigue-testing, climate-control and simulation resources, although access and suitability for the proposed specimens require confirmation.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models

constraints.text: Test specimens and models must represent the painted mild-steel hollow sections and the actual crossmember-to-stringer connection, rather than substitute unrelated welded plate details.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
we are seeing weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections

constraints.text: The investigation must distinguish representative chilled, thermal-cycling and moisture exposure from room-temperature loading; vibration and loading histories must be established rather than assumed.

sources.quote: Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts is doing something we are not seeing at ambient conditions.

constraints.text: The evidence and sampling plan must account for the limited retained failed material and use the available site documentation.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: Combined cold cyclic-load testing requires externally coordinated equipment access; the company cannot currently perform it, and the researcher’s shared equipment must be booked in advance.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: Company engineering effort must be explicitly allocated around live projects because there is no dedicated R&D team.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

risks: The strongest cited thermal-fatigue evidence concerns other steel grades, joint geometries and substantially colder temperature excursions. It does not establish a temperature-driven failure mechanism at 2–6 °C; transfer must be tested in the first representative comparison.

Condensation and coating-related corrosion are company hypotheses, not mechanisms validated by the supplied researcher evidence. Moisture-control capability and any need for corrosion expertise remain unconfirmed.
Only two failed sections are retained. Destructive examination could consume scarce evidence, and unavailable service histories could prevent reliable reproduction of the roughly 18-month failure.
Accelerated testing may change the failure mechanism; any proposed acceleration must be checked against field fracture features before using it to compare modifications.
Researcher availability, committed equipment slots, company budget and target completion date are unknown. Shared facilities and competing company project work could delay the campaign.
Company agreement to the proposed joint-project arrangement and its ability to fund instrumentation, specimens and testing are not established.
questions: Can Erić confirm availability, a named project team and bookable chamber/machine time for a joint project, and can AutomVoj confirm this collaboration format?
What budget, decision deadline and company engineering time can be committed?
Can the two failed sections and site records be released for examination, and what destructive sampling is permitted?
What are the steel grade, wall thickness, joint drawings, filler, welding procedure, inspection records and coating specification for failed and unaffected frames?
Can representative customer installations be instrumented for joint strain, vibration, belt loading, temperature and humidity, including starts, stops, washdown and defrost events?
Can the available rig accommodate representative joints, reproduce the measured load spectrum at 2–6 °C and control condensation safely, or is additional equipment or expertise needed?
Which initial matched test conditions, replication level and field-to-laboratory fracture comparisons will establish whether the published methods transfer before testing design changes?
What evidence will AutomVoj require to adopt a welding, filler or geometry change, and which applicable design and welding requirements must that change satisfy?
